saa-ini-135.text: A team is choosing the type of instance EC2 for three different workloads: (1) an in-memory database server that processes large data sets in RAM, (2) a video processing cluster that performs intensive calculations of CPU, and (3) a simple web server with moderate traffic and balanced use of CPU/memory. What a combination of families of instances EC2 is more suitable for these three loads, respectively?
options: Optimized computer (C) for the in-memory bank, general purpose (T/M) for video processing, and optimized memory (R) for the web server
General purpose (T/M families) for all three loads, as they offer the best balance for any scenario
Optimized memory (family R) for the in-memory bank, optimized computing (family C) for video processing, and general purpose (family T/M) for the web server
Optimized storage (Families I/D) for all three loads, as they offer the best overall performance
saa-ini-135.explanation: Correct. R family instances offer high memory/vCPU ratio, ideal for in-memory banks; the C family offers high processing capacity, ideal for intensive loads of CPU as video processing; and T/M families offer the appropriate balance for moderate traffic web servers.
saa-ini-135.hint: Think of the ratio between vCPU and memory that each family of instance EC2 offers, and in what resource (memory or CPU) is the limiting factor of each workload.
optionRationales: Correct. R family instances offer high memory/vCPU ratio, ideal for in-memory banks; the C family offers high processing capacity, ideal for intensive loads of CPU as video processing; and T/M families offer the appropriate balance for moderate traffic web servers.

This combination reverses the critical features of each load: the in-memory bank needs high memory ratio/vCPU (family R), and video processing needs high capacity of CPU (family C) — not the other way around.

Optimized storage instances are focused on loads with high local I/O throughput (such as banks) NoSQL which depend on local NVMe disks) — do not represent the best general choice for in-memory banks, processing of CPU or simple web servers.
Although suitable for the web server, general purpose instances are not the ideal choice for loads with specific and intense memory needs (bank in-memory) or CPU (video processing).

saa-ini-136.text: An application stores files CSV of several gigabytes in Amazon S3, but each query of the application needs only a few columns and a subset of lines that meet a specific condition. Currently, the application lowers the entire file to process and filter locally, which is slow and consumes unnecessary bandwidth. S3 allows the application to recover only the necessary data, using an expression SQL simple, without downloading the whole object?
options: S3 Select, which allows you to run queries SQL simple directly on objects CSV, JSON or Parquet stored in S3, returning only the requested data
S3 Transfer Acceleration, which speeds up the download of the entire file using the edge locations of the CloudFront
S3 Multipart Upload, which divides the file into parts for parallel upload
S3 Batch Operations, which performs a mass operation on a list of objects
saa-ini-136.explanation: Correct. S3 Select lets you run an expression SQL simple directly on the content of an object CSV, JSON or Parquet, returning only the requested columns/lines, without the entire object having to be transferred.
saa-ini-136.hint: Think about the resource of S3 which allows to use an expression SQL simple to return only the necessary columns/lines of an object, without lowering it completely.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Select lets you run an expression SQL simple directly on the content of an object CSV, JSON or Parquet, returning only the requested columns/lines, without the entire object having to be transferred.
Transfer Acceleration accelerates the transfer of the entire object through the edge locations — it does not filter or return only a subset of the contents of the object.
Multipart Upload is a resource for uploading large objects into parallel parts — it has nothing to do with consulting or filtering the content of an object during reading.
The S3 Batch Operations performs an action (such as copying or tagging) on a large list of objects — not designed to filter the internal content of a single object during reading.

saa-ini-137.text: One API REST built with Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda receives a large volume of identical requests (even endpoints, same parameters) for a resource whose result changes only every few minutes. At each request, a new invocation of the function Lambda and a new search of the database is carried out, generating unnecessary cost and latency. API Gateway can reduce the number of invocations from Lambda and latency for these repeated requests?
options: Enable cache of API Gateway to the stage of the API, defining a life time (TTL) for the cache responses of each endpoint combination and parameters
Configure the API Gateway to use authentication IAM instead of keys for API
Increase the timeout set for the function Lambda
Migration to API of REST API for HTTP API, which is always faster
saa-ini-137.explanation: Correct. API Gateway temporarily stores endpoint responses by a TTL configurable; identical requests within this period are met by the cache, without invoking the Lambda nor consult the bank again.
saa-ini-137.hint: Think about the resource of API Gateway that temporarily stores endpoint responses, avoiding repeated calls to the backend for identical requests within a defined period.
optionRationales: Correct. API Gateway temporarily stores endpoint responses by a TTL configurable; identical requests within this period are met by the cache, without invoking the Lambda nor consult the bank again.
Increasing the timeout only allows the execution to take longer before it fails — does not reduce the number of calls or avoid repeated queries to the database.
The authentication method used by API is not related to cache storage of responses and does not reduce the number of invocations of Lambda.
HTTP APIs can be faster and cheaper in general, but this does not replace the answer cache — without cache, each identical request would continue to invoke the Lambda and consulting the database.

saa-ini-138.text: An account of AWS performs various functions Lambda. One of them, responsible for processing critical payments, needs to ensure that it always has the capacity to execute available, even if other functions in the same account consume much of the limit of competition of the account during peaks of traffic. Lambda ensures that this critical function always has a minimum number of simultaneous performances available, isolating it from the competitive consumption of other functions?
options: Set up reserved competition for the payment function, with a part of the account's limit of competition reserved exclusively for it
Increase the memory allocated to the payment function
Configure a Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) for the payment function
Publish a new version of the payment function
saa-ini-138.explanation: The reserved competition reserves part of the account's limit of competition exclusively for the specified function, ensuring that it always has available capacity, isolated from the consumption of other functions.
saa-ini-138.hint: Think about the configuration of Lambda which reserves a part of the account's limit of competition exclusively for a specific function, excluding it from other functions.
optionRationales: The reserved competition reserves part of the account's limit of competition exclusively for the specified function, ensuring that it always has available capacity, isolated from the consumption of other functions.

Increasing memory improves the resources of CPU/memory available for CADA individual execution, but does not reserve or isolate a set of simultaneous executions in relation to other account functions.
One DLQ capture events that failed after exhausting repetition attempts — it does not reserve simultaneous execution capacity for function.
Publishing versions manages the code life cycle and implementation aliases — this does not isolate or reserve competition over other account functions.

saa-ini-139.text: An instance EC2 executes an application with intense use of I/O in volumes EBS with Provisioned IOPS (The team realizes that, at times of high network traffic for other purposes (such as replication of data outside the instance), the performance of the EBS falls significantly, suggesting that the general network traffic of the instance is competing with traffic for volumes EBS for the same network capacity. What can be configured to ensure network capacity DEDICADA for traffic EBS, separate from the general network traffic of the instance?
options: Increase volume size EBS, without changing the type of instance
Migrate volumes EBS from i2 to gp3
Use an instance enabled as 'EBS-optimized', which provides dedicated network capacity for traffic between instance and volumes EBS
Deactivate volume encryption EBS to reduce overhead
saa-ini-139.explanation: Correct. 'EBS-optimized' provide dedicated and separate network capacity specifically for traffic with volumes EBS, avoiding that it competes with the general network traffic of the instance.
saa-ini-139.hint: Think about the feature of some instances EC2 providing dedicated and separate network capacity specifically for traffic with volumes EBS.
optionRationales: Correct. 'EBS-optimized' provide dedicated and separate network capacity specifically for traffic with volumes EBS, avoiding that it competes with the general network traffic of the instance.

Increasing volume size does not resolve a network bandwidth dispute between traffic EBS and the general network traffic of the instance — the limit is in the network capacity of the instance, not in the size of the volume.
Changing the volume type does not solve a network bandwidth containment problem at the instance level — the described gargal is in shared network capacity, not in volume type.
The cryptographic overhead of EBS is minimal and not related to network bandwidth containment between traffic EBS and general instance network traffic.

saa-ini-140.text: Courts EC2 in private subnets of a VPC frequently access the Amazon S3 to read and record large volumes of data. Currently, this traffic passes through a NAT Gateway up to the public internet to reach the S3, generating data processing costs from the NAT Gateway and additional latency. VPC allows such traffic to the S3 remain within the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway or on the public internet, reducing cost and latency?
options: An Elastic IP assigned to each instance EC2
Increase the size of NAT Gateway to support more bandwidth
One VPC Peering with another VPC containing the bucket S3
One VPC Gateway-type endpoint for the Amazon S3, added to the private subnet route table
saa-ini-140.explanation: Right. VPC Gateway-type endpoint for the S3 (or DynamoDB) is added directly to the sub-network route table, allowing traffic for these services to remain in the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway or on the Internet, without additional cost per hour or per processed data.
saa-ini-140.hint: Think about the type of VPC Endpoint that allows private subnet traffic to Amazon S3 (and DynamoDB) remain in the network of AWS, being added directly to the route table, without cost per hour or per processed data.
optionRationales: Right. VPC Gateway-type endpoint for the S3 (or DynamoDB) is added directly to the sub-network route table, allowing traffic for these services to remain in the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway or on the Internet, without additional cost per hour or per processed data.
Buckets S3 do not reside 'within' a VPC; o VPC Peering connects VPCs to each other and is not the way to access the S3 directly from the network of the AWS without going through the Internet.

Assigning Elastic IPs gives public IP addresses to instances, but does not avoid the way through NAT Gateway does not resolve the additional cost and latency to access the S3 from private sub-networks.
NAT Gateways do not have a configurable 'size' in this way, and even increasing capacity, traffic would continue to generate data processing cost and additional latency when passing through it.

saa-ini-141.text: A site has two categories of content: images of products, which rarely change, and a file JSON with the stock count, which is updated every few seconds. Both are served through the same distribution of the Amazon CloudFront, but currently configured with the same TTL of a kind used in the manufacture of 24 hours, making users see outdated stock information. What the architect should set up to solve this while taking advantage of the cache for the images?
options: Reduce or TTL of the whole distribution for a few seconds, applying it also to the images
Disable cache from CloudFront completely and serve everything directly from the origin
Create different behavior caches for each path pattern, defining a TTL long for the images and a TTL short (or cache disabled) for the stock file
Create a second distribution CloudFront identical only to the stock file
saa-ini-141.explanation: Correct. Cache behaviors allow you to set different cache rules — including TTL — for different path patterns within the same distribution, allowing to keep long cache for images and short cache (or disabled) only for the stock file.
saa-ini-141.hint: Think about the resource of CloudFront which allows you to set cache rules (including TTL) different for different path patterns within the same distribution.
optionRationales: Correct. Cache behaviors allow you to set different cache rules — including TTL — for different path patterns within the same distribution, allowing to keep long cache for images and short cache (or disabled) only for the stock file.

This would resolve the stock outdated, but would drastically reduce the cache's benefit to the images, increasing the load on the origin and latency without need — something that caches separate behaviors avoid.
Disable the cache completely eliminates the benefit of CloudFront for images, which rarely change and benefit greatly from a long-term cache.
Creating a separate whole distribution is an unnecessary complexity — cache behaviors within a single distribution already solve this requirement directly.

saa-ini-142.text: A company needs to migrate 80 data terabytes from your data center on-premises for the Amazon S3. The Internet connection available has limited capacity, and the network transfer would take more than a month. AWS is more suitable to accelerate this initial migration of large volume of data?
options: Compress files before upload using the AWS CLI
AWS Snowball Edge, a physical storage device sent to the company to load the data locally and returned to AWS for import S3
Increase the number of parallel connections used by S3 Transfer Acceleration
AWS Direct Connect, hiring a link of greater capacity only for this transfer
saa-ini-142.explanation: Correct. AWS Snowball Edge is a robust physical storage device, sent to the customer, used to transfer large volumes of data (such as 80 TB) without depending on the limited capacity of the internet connection — the data are loaded locally and imported into S3 after the device returns to AWS.
saa-ini-142.hint: Think of the service of AWS involving the sending of a physical storage device to the customer, for the physical transport of large volumes of data without depending on the network.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Snowball Edge is a robust physical storage device, sent to the customer, used to transfer large volumes of data (such as 80 TB) without depending on the limited capacity of the internet connection — the data are loaded locally and imported into S3 after the device returns to AWS.

Provide a new connection Direct Connect usually takes weeks to months to establish and is focused on continuous connectivity — is not a practical solution to accelerate a single and urgent data transfer.
The S3 Transfer Acceleration still depends on the total capacity of the same limited internet connection — multiple parallel connections do not exceed the aggregate band limit available.
Compression may reduce the volume of data, but it is unlikely that it will reduce 80 TB enough to make a transfer of more than a month, in a limited, practical link.

saa-ini-143.text: A real-time network package processing application run in instances EC2, needs very high rate of packages per second (PPS), low network latency between instances and minimum jitter. The team wants to take advantage of an optimized network feature, available in modern instances, to meet this requirement. Which feature should be enabled/used?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration in instances
Enhanced Networking (using the Elastic Network Adapter driver) - ENA), available in supported instance types, which offers higher rate of packages per second, lower latency and lower jitter
Migrate instances to a public sub-network
Increase volume size EBS attached to the bodies
saa-ini-143.explanation: Correct. Enhanced Networking, enabled via driver ENA in supported instance types, offers significantly higher per second package rates, lower latency between instances and lower jitter, compared to the standard network driver..
saa-ini-143.hint: Think of the optimized network feature, based on a specific network adapter driver, available in modern instance types for high network performance.
optionRationales: Correct. Enhanced Networking, enabled via driver ENA in supported instance types, offers significantly higher per second package rates, lower latency between instances and lower jitter, compared to the standard network driver..
Volume size EBS is related to storage capacity — is not related to the rate of packages per second or network latency between instances.
The S3 Transfer Acceleration accelerates transfers to/from S3 using the internet edge locations — has no relation to network performance between instances EC2.
Public or private sub-networks determine Internet accessibility, not the rate of packages per second or network latency between instances.

saa-ini-144.text: A company has hundreds of instances EC2 and wants to identify, based on the actual history of use of CPU, memory and network (collected by CloudWatch), which instances are over or undersized, receiving recommendations of types of instance more suitable for the observed use profile. AWS generates this type of automated recommendation based on machine learning?
options: Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights
AWS Optimizer Computers
AWS Configure
AWS Cost Explorer
saa-ini-144.explanation: Correct. AWS Computer Optimizer analyzes historical metrics of use of CPU, memory, network and other resources collected by CloudWatch and uses machine learning to recommend instance types (EC2, among other resources) better suited to the observed use profile.
saa-ini-144.hint: Think of the service of AWS analyzing historical metrics of use (CPU, memory, network) and use machine learning to recommend more appropriate instance types.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Computer Optimizer analyzes historical metrics of use of CPU, memory, network and other resources collected by CloudWatch and uses machine learning to recommend instance types (EC2, among other resources) better suited to the observed use profile.
The CloudWatch Logs Insights is a consultation tool on logs — it does not generate recommendations for sizing instance types based on usage metrics.

The AWS Cost Explorer focus on visualization and cost and usage forecasting — it does not generate recommendations for dimensioning machine learning-based instances about patterns of use of CPU/memory/network.
The AWS Config evaluates the configuration of resources in relation to compliance rules — it does not analyze usage patterns to generate sizing recommendations.
